page: UpCloud PREMIUM-64xCPU-384GB is a KVM-hypervised virtual server built on the x86_64 architecture. It features an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz, configured with 64 physical cores and 64 vCPUs under a shared CPU allocation model. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, yielding 6.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided via a bundled 500 GB local SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. The processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, vector neural network instructions (AVX512_VNNI), bfloat16 (AVX512_BF16), and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates top-tier performance in both single-core and multi-core computational tasks. Stress-ng and Geekbench scores place the CPU capabilities in the top 10% of tested hardware, with strong multi-threaded decompression and software compilation metrics. However, a performance tradeoff is observed in memory operations. While cached small-block read bandwidth is in the top tier at 8129.22 GB/sec, large-block uncached read and write memory bandwidths fall into the average category at 178.6 GB/sec and 78.06 GB/sec respectively. Similarly, the PassMark memory score is positioned in the middle 50% of benchmarks.

This server configuration is highly suited for compute-heavy workloads, software compilation, ray tracing, and database operations. It delivers strong performance for Redis SET operations and static web serving. For machine learning, the hardware achieves top-tier prompt processing speeds for small LLM models, though text generation speeds for medium models remain in the top 25% range. Given its high core density and balanced memory-to-CPU ratio, the instance offers qualitative cost efficiency for resource-intensive enterprise applications that require substantial parallel processing power without the need for dedicated GPU acceleration.
